title: Spreading the fixed costs

predict.q: The bakery doubles output from 50 to 100 cakes a day. Fixed costs stay at £300. What happens to **fixed cost per cake**?

options.fb: £300 shared by twice as many cakes: £6 → £3 per cake.
Total fixed cost stays at £300. Spread over twice as many cakes, each cake carries half as much.
The total stays the same, but the cost per cake does not: 300 ÷ 50 = £6, 300 ÷ 100 = £3.
Fixed cost per cake falls but never reaches zero: £300 must still be shared out.

task: Move the **output** slider from 50 to 200 and watch fixed cost per cake, variable cost per cake and average cost.

target.do: Move the output slider to 100, then press Check.

takeaway: Fixed cost per unit keeps falling as output rises; average cost falls at first, then can rise again as variable cost per unit climbs.
